Uniform early-time O((1+t)^(-1/2)) variation and large-time Fourier gap O(n^(-1) exp(-8t/n²)) suppress t/n²→0,∞. On t=sn² compact windows Fourier modes converge uniformly to a periodized Gaussian derivative; shifted Riemann sums give s∫|h_s′|. Jacobi triple product establishes strict decrease on the semicircle and the odd theta series G(u)=u∑_{k odd≥1}e^(-k²u). Independent finite Poisson/Fourier samples n=32,64,128,256 converge, not proofs. Hilbert normal multipliers optimize to 1/(e sin(π/n)), consistent also n=2.
